OIL LEAKS CHECK

All OK

Problems encountered

Operation

Raise the vehicle on a two column lift and check that there are no oil leaks from the shock absorber stem.

the check on the shock absorber should only be carried out after driving on a dry road, slight dampness of the stem is considered normal since this is due to evaporation that takes place during the operation of the shock absorber.

If there is a persistent oil leak on the shock absorber stem, make sure that it is not coming from other parts of the vehicle that are lubricated

Move on to Step 2

Leaks from other parts that are lubricated

Search for the cause of the leak following the appropriate diagnostic procedure

Leaks from the shock absorber stem

Replace the shock absorber

HANDBRAKE CHECK

All OK

Problems encountered

Operation

Check that the handbrake cables or outer casing do not knock against the fuel tank, heat shields or bodywork during oscillations.

Move on to Step 3

Inteference between outer casing or cables and other elements

Cover the outer casing with foam rubber tape in the area of the interference or lubricate the cable

3

INTERFERENCE CHECK

All OK

Problems encountered

Operation

Check that there are no signs of interference between the suspension elements or between the latter and the bodyshell. In particular, check that there are no signs of wear on the suspension springs and that they do not show signs of abrasion.

If the spring shows signs of abrasion, its mechanical properties could be weakened as a result of oxidation.

Move on to Step 4

Inteference due to incorrect fitting.

Eliminate the interference and restore the correct fastening. If this is not possible, replace the defective components

Abrasions or non conformity of the spring

Replace the spring

Op. 4420A12 REAR SUSPENSION DAMPER (ONE), LH OR RH - FOR MCPHERSON STRUT SYSTEM - INCLUDES DISMENTLING/REBUILDING OF ASSEMBLY AT BENCH - R.R.

taking care to fit it correctly

TIGHTENING TORQUE CHECK

All OK

Problems encountered

Operation

Locate the area of the possible noise source: top or bottom.

Starting from the area where the knocking was identified, check

See Test 4420OB CHECK ON CORRECT TIGHTENINGS FOR REAR SUSPENSION

the tightening torques of the non-yield point type fixing bolts:

- the shock absorber shim;

- the lower mounting of the shock absorber to the longitudinal track control arm;

- the transverse plate to the longitudinal arm;

- the bracket fastening the longitudinal arm to the body;

- the fastening for the bush to the longitudinal arm;

- the anti-roll bar to the crossmember;

- the connecting rod to the bar and to the longitudinal arm;

- the camber rod to the steering knuckle;

(only for the 2.2 JTS) - the rear fastening of the longitudinal arm to the steering knuckle;

(only for the 3.2 V6 engine) - the rear differential fastening to the crossmember;

- the brake caliper to steering knuckle;

- the brake disc guard to the steering knuckle;

- the steering knuckle to the hub.

Visually inspect that the yield point type bolts have not loosened, the list is given below:

- the shock absorber bracket to the bodyshell;

- the camber rod to the crossmember;

- the transverse plate to the crossmember;

- the longitudinal arm bush to the mounting bracket on the bodyshell;

- the front fastening for the longitudinal arm to the steering knuckle;

- the crossmember to the bodyshell.

Move on to Step 5

Non-shear bolts not tightened to torque

Restore the correct tightness

Shear bolts loosened

Replace the shear bolts and restore the correct tightness
